candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Distance represents a numerical value combined with a unit of length. Also called length, extent, span, separation. Examples: "10 km", "5 miles", "300 meters", "2 feet".

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

types.embedding_query_text: Journalist: A person who collects, writes, or distributes news or other current information. Also called Reporter, Correspondent, Writer, Columnist. Examples: Vic Hood, Freelance video games journalist Vic Hood.

chosen_type.label: Journalist
chosen_type.definition: A person who collects, writes, or distributes news or other current information.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate directly represents a journalist. 'Journalist' is a profession, making 'Occupation' the most appropriate parent for this new type.

candidates.label: ReportageNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A ReportageNewsArticle is a NewsArticle representing news articles based on factual journalistic reporting, emphasizing verified information and multiple viewpoints. Also called news report, journalistic article, factual news. Examples: a breaking news story about a political event, an investigative report on a social issue, a factual account of a natural disaster, a report on scientific findings. Distinct from AnalysisNewsArticle, which goes deeper into analysis.

candidates.label: NewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle, as an Article, is a creative work whose content reports news or provides background context for understanding news. Also called news report, news story, journalistic article. Examples: a breaking news report, an investigative journalism piece, an opinion column in a newspaper. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically less formal and often personal.

candidates.label: BackgroundNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle that provides historical context, definitions, or detailed explanations on a specific topic. Also called explainer article, backgrounder, FAQ document. Examples: "An explainer on climate change", "A detailed history of the European Union", "FAQ about blockchain technology". Distinct from NewsArticle, which reports on current events.

candidates.label: ReviewNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A specialized news article that combines factual reporting with a professional critic's assessment of a service, product, performance, or artistic work. Also called critical news report, professional review article, news critique. Examples: a New York Times review of a Broadway show, a tech blog's assessment of a new smartphone, a music magazine's album critique.

candidates.label: AnalysisNewsArticle
candidates.comment: An AnalysisNewsArticle is a NewsArticle that combines factual reporting with the author's expertise, offering interpretations and conclusions. Also called news analysis, interpretive news, expert commentary. Examples: An article analyzing the economic impact of a new policy, a piece interpreting election results, a report on scientific findings with expert commentary. Distinct from NewsArticle, which primarily focuses on factual reporting without extensive interpretation.

types.embedding_query_text: Entrepreneur: A person who organizes and operates a business or businesses, taking on greater than normal financial risks in order to do so. Also called Businessman, Businesswoman, Innovator, Founder. Examples: Sir Ian Livingstone, British gaming entrepreneur Sir Ian Livingstone.

chosen_type.label: Entrepreneur
chosen_type.definition: A person who organizes and operates a business or businesses, taking on greater than normal financial risks in order to do so.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate directly represents an entrepreneur. 'Entrepreneur' is a profession, making 'Occupation' the most appropriate parent for this new type.

candidates.label: EntertainmentBusiness
candidates.comment: An EntertainmentBusiness is a LocalBusiness that provides entertainment services. Also called amusement business, leisure provider. Examples: A movie theater, a concert venue, an arcade, a theme park.

candidates.label: LocalBusiness
candidates.comment: A specific physical business or a branch of an organization that serves a local community. Also called local company, neighborhood business, regional enterprise. Examples: a local restaurant, a bank branch, a medical clinic, a bowling alley, a grocery store. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group of people with a particular purpose.

candidates.label: Casino
candidates.comment: A local business primarily offering gambling activities and often entertainment. Also called gambling house, gaming establishment, resort casino. Examples: Bellagio, Caesars Palace, Monte Carlo Casino.

candidates.label: OnlineBusiness
candidates.comment: An OnlineBusiness is a particular business that operates primarily or entirely online. Also called e-business, internet business, digital enterprise. Examples: an e-commerce site, an online travel agency, a virtual doctor's office. Distinct from LocalBusiness, which has a physical presence.

candidates.label: MedicalBusiness
candidates.comment: A local business operating for medical purposes, which can be physical or virtual. Also called healthcare business, medical practice, health services provider. Examples: a dental office, a physical therapy clinic, a telemedicine service, a diagnostic lab. Distinct from LocalBusiness, which is a broader category for any local business.

types.embedding_query_text: RadioProgram: A broadcast segment or series of segments on radio. Also called Radio show, Broadcast, Program. Examples: BBC's Today programme.

chosen_type.label: RadioSeries
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org RadioSeries class, defined as a 'radio program series', is a perfect match for 'BBC's Today programme' and the OIE_TYPE definition.

candidates.label: RadioSeries
candidates.comment: A RadioSeries is a CreativeWorkSeries dedicated to radio broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called radio show, radio program series. Examples: "The Archers", "This American Life", a long-running radio drama, a daily news radio program.

candidates.label: RadioSeason
candidates.comment: A RadioSeason is a CreativeWorkSeason dedicated to radio broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called radio series season. Examples: Season 1 of a radio drama, a specific year's collection of a weekly radio show, a themed season of a podcast broadcast on radio.

candidates.label: RadioClip
candidates.comment: A RadioClip is a Clip representing a short radio program or a segment of a radio program. Also called radio segment, audio clip, radio excerpt. Examples: a news report from a radio show, a short interview clip, a commercial break, a song played on the radio.

candidates.label: RadioBroadcastService
candidates.comment: A RadioBroadcastService is a BroadcastService delivering radio content via broadcast over the air or online. Also called radio service, broadcast radio. Examples: BBC Radio 4, NPR, a local FM radio station, an internet radio stream.

candidates.label: RadioEpisode
candidates.comment: A RadioEpisode is an Episode representing a single installment of a radio series or season. Also called radio show episode, audio episode. Examples: an episode of "This American Life", a specific installment of a radio drama, a segment of a daily news program.

types.embedding_query_text: LaunchDate: The scheduled or actual date when a product, service, or event is first introduced or made available. Also called Release date, Debut date, Introduction date. Examples: game's pre-sales launch date.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: A 'launch date' is a specific calendar date, which is accurately represented by the schema.org Date data type.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: PreOrderAction
candidates.comment: PreOrderAction is a TradeAction where an agent orders an object, product, or service that is not yet released, for future delivery. Also called pre-booking, advance ordering. Examples: pre-ordering a new video game, reserving an upcoming book, pre-booking a new car model, ordering a limited edition item before release.

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

candidates.label: ShippingDeliveryTime
candidates.comment: A structured value providing details about the expected delivery times for product shipping. Also called delivery timeframe, estimated delivery, shipping lead time, transit time. Examples: 'ships in 1-2 business days', 'delivery by Friday', 'estimated 3-5 day transit'.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

types.embedding_query_text: Artwork: A piece of art, such as a painting, sculpture, or design. Also called Art piece, Design, Illustration, Visual art. Examples: cover art.

chosen_type.label: CoverArt
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org CoverArt class is a direct and accurate match for the OIE_TYPE definition and the example 'cover art'.

candidates.label: CoverArt
candidates.comment: CoverArt is the visual artwork displayed on the outer surface of a CreativeWork, such as a book, album, or magazine. Also called album cover, book jacket, magazine cover, artwork. Examples: The cover of "Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band," the dust jacket of "To Kill a Mockingbird," the poster for a movie.

candidates.label: VisualArtwork
candidates.comment: A creative work that is primarily visual in nature, such as a painting, sculpture, or photograph. Also called art piece, visual art, artwork. Examples: Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa, a Rodin sculpture, an Ansel Adams photograph.

candidates.label: Painting
candidates.comment: A Painting, as a CreativeWork, is an artwork created by applying paint to a surface. Also called artwork, canvas, oil painting. Examples: Leonardo da Vinci's 'Mona Lisa', a watercolor landscape, an abstract acrylic painting. Distinct from Photograph, which is an image captured by a camera.

candidates.label: Sculpture
candidates.comment: A three-dimensional work of art created by shaping or combining materials. Also called statue, carving, monument, artwork. Examples: Michelangelo's David, Rodin's The Thinker, a modern abstract metal sculpture, a clay bust.

candidates.label: Book
candidates.comment: A CreativeWork consisting of a written or printed work, typically bound together and protected by a cover. Also called publication, volume, printed matter. Examples: "To Kill a Mockingbird", "The Lord of the Rings", "A textbook on physics". Distinct from BookSeries, which is a collection of books.

types.embedding_query_text: Cost: The amount of money required to buy, make, or do something. Also called Expense, Price, Expenditure, Outlay. Examples: development costs.

chosen_type.label: MonetaryAmount
chosen_type.justification: The OIE_TYPE 'Cost' refers to an amount of money, which is best represented by the schema.org MonetaryAmount class, as seen in the example 'development costs'.

candidates.label: PriceTypeEnumeration
candidates.comment: PriceTypeEnumeration is an Enumeration listing different types of prices, such as list price, invoice price, or sale price. Also called pricing category, cost type. Examples: list price, sale price, invoice price, suggested retail price.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: Demand
candidates.comment: An intangible entity representing a public announcement by an organization or person seeking specific goods or services. Also called Request for goods, wanted ad, procurement request, call for bids. Examples: A company seeking bids for a new IT system, a person looking to buy a specific vintage car, a job posting for a software engineer. Distinct from Offer, which is an announcement to provide goods or services.

candidates.label: PriceComponentTypeEnumeration
candidates.comment: PriceComponentTypeEnumeration is an Enumeration listing different types of price components that collectively form the total price of an offered product. Also called price element type, cost breakdown category. Examples: base price, tax, shipping fee, discount.

candidates.label: Invoice
candidates.comment: An Invoice is an intangible statement detailing the money due for goods or services; a bill. Also called bill, statement of account, charge slip. Examples: a utility bill, a contractor's invoice for services, a restaurant check.

types.embedding_query_text: Duration: The length of time that something continues or lasts. Also called Period, Length of time, Span, Interval. Examples: extra months.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Duration class is a direct and accurate match for the OIE_TYPE definition and the example 'extra months'.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: ServicePeriod
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

types.embedding_query_text: GameContent: Additional items, features, or elements available within a video game. Also called In-game items, DLC, Extra features, Bonus content. Examples: extra vehicles and weapons.

chosen_type.label: GameContent
chosen_type.definition: Additional items, features, or elements available within a video game.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate directly represents general game content. 'Extra vehicles and weapons' are creative elements within a game, making 'CreativeWork' an appropriate parent.

candidates.label: WebContent
candidates.comment: A general type representing any content accessible via the web, including web pages, websites, and their elements. Also called web content item, online content, digital web asset. Examples: a blog post, an entire website, an image embedded on a page.

candidates.label: VideoGameClip
candidates.comment: A short segment or part of a video game, often used for promotional or highlight purposes. Also called game clip, gameplay footage, video game segment. Examples: a highlight reel from an e-sports match, a trailer showing a game's cutscene, a short recording of a player's achievement.

candidates.label: VideoGameSeries
candidates.comment: A sequence of related video games, often sharing a common storyline, characters, or gameplay mechanics. Also called game franchise, video game saga, game series. Examples: The Final Fantasy series, The Elder Scrolls series, Grand Theft Auto series.

candidates.label: TechArticle
candidates.comment: An article providing technical information, such as how-to guides, troubleshooting steps, or specifications. Also called technical guide, how-to article, procedural document, specification. Examples: an article on 'How to install Linux', a troubleshooting guide for a software error, a specification document for a new API.

candidates.label: VideoGame
candidates.comment: An electronic game that involves human interaction with a user interface to generate visual feedback on a video device. Also called computer game, console game, digital game. Examples: Super Mario Bros., The Legend of Zelda, Call of Duty.

types.embedding_query_text: DigitalProduct: A product that is stored, delivered, and used in electronic format. Also called Electronic product, Software, Digital good, Downloadable content. Examples: digital download.

chosen_type.label: DigitalProduct
chosen_type.definition: A product that is stored, delivered, and used in electronic format.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate directly represents a digital product. A 'digital download' is a type of product, making 'Product' the most appropriate parent for this new type.

candidates.label: DigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A creative work representing an electronic file or document. Also called Electronic document, e-document, digital file, computer file. Examples: A PDF report, a Word document, a spreadsheet, an image file, an e-book. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is a broader category for any creative output.

candidates.label: FinancialProduct
candidates.comment: A FinancialProduct is a Service provided by financial institutions to consumers and businesses. Also called financial instrument, banking product, investment product. Examples: A savings account, a mortgage loan, an insurance policy, a mutual fund.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: TextDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A digital document primarily composed of textual content. Also called text file, digital document, e-document. Examples: a PDF report, a Word document, an e-book. Distinct from TextObject, which is a media object representing a text file, often for embedding or linking.

types.embedding_query_text: GameMode: A distinct way of playing a video game, often with different rules or objectives. Also called Play mode, Game type, Mode of play. Examples: online mode.

chosen_type.label: GamePlayMode
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org GamePlayMode enumeration categorizes ways of playing a game, which aligns well with the OIE_TYPE 'GameMode' and the example 'online mode'.

candidates.label: GamePlayMode
candidates.comment: A GamePlayMode is an Enumeration indicating whether a game is multi-player, co-op, or single-player. Also called player mode, game type. Examples: SinglePlayer, MultiPlayer, CoOp.

candidates.label: Game
candidates.comment: A Game is a CreativeWork representing a rule-governed recreational activity, often involving players assuming roles in a fictional setting. Also called pastime, play, recreational activity. Examples: A board game like Chess, a video game like Minecraft, a role-playing game like Dungeons & Dragons, a card game like Poker.

candidates.label: VideoGame
candidates.comment: An electronic game that involves human interaction with a user interface to generate visual feedback on a video device. Also called computer game, console game, digital game. Examples: Super Mario Bros., The Legend of Zelda, Call of Duty.

candidates.label: PlayGameAction
candidates.comment: PlayGameAction is a ConsumeAction specifically representing the act of playing a video game. Also called gaming, video gaming, playing a digital game. Examples: playing "Minecraft", playing "Fortnite", playing "Chess" online, playing a mobile game. Distinct from PlayAction, which is a broader act of playing or performing.

candidates.label: GameServer
candidates.comment: A GameServer is an Intangible server that facilitates game interaction in a multiplayer game. Also called game host, multiplayer server. Examples: A dedicated server for an online game, a private game server for friends, a public game server for a large community.

types.embedding_query_text: Legislation: Laws and regulations made by a legislative body. Also called Law, Statute, Regulation, Act. Examples: age verification legislation.

chosen_type.label: Legislation
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Legislation class is a direct and accurate match for the OIE_TYPE definition and the example 'age verification legislation'.

candidates.label: Legislation
candidates.comment: Legislation is a creative work representing a legal document such as an act, decree, or bill, or a component thereof. Also called law, statute, legal act, regulation. Examples: the Civil Rights Act, a local ordinance, a proposed bill in parliament. Distinct from LegislationObject, which is a specific file containing the legislation.

candidates.label: LegislationObject
candidates.comment: A LegislationObject is a specific file or object containing a Legislation, which can exist in multiple formats. Also called legal document file, legislation artifact, law document. Examples: a PDF of a specific law, an HTML version of a regulation, a digitally signed legal document. Distinct from Legislation, which is the abstract legal document itself.

candidates.label: LegalValueLevel
candidates.comment: LegalValueLevel is an enumeration of possible levels for the legal validity or authority of a legislation. Also called legislative authority level, legal hierarchy, law's binding power. Examples: 'Primary', 'Secondary', 'Tertiary', 'Advisory'.

candidates.label: LegalForceStatus
candidates.comment: LegalForceStatus is an enumeration of possible statuses for the legal force or validity of a legislation. Also called legal validity status, legislative effect, law status. Examples: 'InForce', 'Repealed', 'Expired', 'Pending'.

candidates.label: LegislativeBuilding
candidates.comment: A LegislativeBuilding is a government building civic structure where legislative bodies meet and conduct their work. Also called capitol building, parliament house, assembly hall. Examples: the U.S. Capitol, a state capitol building, the Houses of Parliament. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

types.embedding_query_text: Platform: A system or environment that enables the operation of software or services. Also called System, Framework, Environment, Service. Examples: social media.

chosen_type.label: Platform
chosen_type.definition: A system or environment that enables the operation of software or services.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate directly represents a general 'Platform' like 'social media'. 'Thing' is the most appropriate general parent for this new, broad concept.

candidates.label: DigitalPlatformEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration listing common technology platforms, used to specify where an action or content is available. Also called Technology platform, software platform, operating system, device type. Examples: iOS, Android, Web, Desktop, Console. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is the application itself, not the platform it runs on.

candidates.label: RuntimePlatform
candidates.comment: A specialized software environment providing the necessary infrastructure, libraries, and services for executing a program. Also called execution environment, software platform, runtime environment, operating system. Examples: Java Virtual Machine (JVM), Node.js runtime, .NET Common Language Runtime (CLR), Python interpreter.

candidates.label: OperatingSystem
candidates.comment: An OperatingSystem, as a SoftwareApplication, is system software that manages computer hardware and software resources. Also called OS, system software, platform. Examples: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is a general application program.

candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

candidates.label: ControlAction
candidates.comment: An action where an agent operates or manages a device or application. Also called controlling, operating, managing, manipulating. Examples: Turning on a light, adjusting a thermostat, launching a software application, steering a car. Distinct from Action, which is a general activity.

types.embedding_query_text: CommunicationFeature: A function or capability within a system that allows users to communicate. Also called Messaging function, Chat feature, Communication tool. Examples: messaging in gaming.

chosen_type.label: CommunicationFeature
chosen_type.definition: A function or capability within a system that allows users to communicate.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate directly represents a communication feature. 'Messaging in gaming' is an intangible capability, making 'Intangible' the most appropriate parent.

candidates.label: CommunicateAction
candidates.comment: The act of transmitting information to another person or entity through a specific medium. Also called communication, conveying information, interacting. Examples: Sending an email, making a phone call, giving a speech, writing a letter. Distinct from InteractAction, which is a broader category of actions involving interaction.

candidates.label: Conversation
candidates.comment: A series of one or more messages exchanged between individuals or organizations on a specific topic. Also called discussion, dialogue, chat, discourse. Examples: An email thread, a text message exchange, a forum discussion, a spoken dialogue. Distinct from Comment, which is a single remark on an item.

candidates.label: Message
candidates.comment: A creative work representing a single communication from a sender to one or more recipients. Also called communication, dispatch, note, email. Examples: an email, a text message, a direct message on social media, a voicemail.

candidates.label: UserComments
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of posting comments or feedback. Also called user comment, public comment, feedback post. Examples: a user leaving a comment on a blog post, posting a review, providing feedback on a product.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

types.embedding_query_text: GameSetting: The fictional world or environment in which a video game's story and gameplay take place. Also called Game world, Fictional environment, Setting. Examples: 3D setting.

chosen_type.label: GameSetting
chosen_type.definition: The fictional world or environment in which a video game's story and gameplay take place.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate directly represents a game setting. A '3D setting' is a fictional environment within a creative work, making 'CreativeWork' an appropriate parent.

candidates.label: Game
candidates.comment: A Game is a CreativeWork representing a rule-governed recreational activity, often involving players assuming roles in a fictional setting. Also called pastime, play, recreational activity. Examples: A board game like Chess, a video game like Minecraft, a role-playing game like Dungeons & Dragons, a card game like Poker.

candidates.label: VideoGameSeries
candidates.comment: A sequence of related video games, often sharing a common storyline, characters, or gameplay mechanics. Also called game franchise, video game saga, game series. Examples: The Final Fantasy series, The Elder Scrolls series, Grand Theft Auto series.

candidates.label: VideoGame
candidates.comment: An electronic game that involves human interaction with a user interface to generate visual feedback on a video device. Also called computer game, console game, digital game. Examples: Super Mario Bros., The Legend of Zelda, Call of Duty.

candidates.label: ShippingRateSettings
candidates.comment: A structured value representing reusable shipping rate information, often linked to an offer via a shipping settings link. Also called shipping cost rules, freight pricing, delivery charges configuration. Examples: a flat rate shipping setting for standard delivery, a weight-based shipping rate table, a zone-based shipping cost.

candidates.label: PlayGameAction
candidates.comment: PlayGameAction is a ConsumeAction specifically representing the act of playing a video game. Also called gaming, video gaming, playing a digital game. Examples: playing "Minecraft", playing "Fortnite", playing "Chess" online, playing a mobile game. Distinct from PlayAction, which is a broader act of playing or performing.

types.embedding_query_text: Adventure: An exciting or unusual experience, often involving risk or danger. Also called Quest, Journey, Exploration, Exploit. Examples: Bonnie and Clyde-esque adventure.

chosen_type.label: Trip
chosen_type.justification: An 'adventure' can be broadly considered a type of journey or experience, which aligns with the schema.org Trip class, an intangible entity representing a journey.

candidates.label: Trip
candidates.comment: A general term for a journey or itinerary involving visits to one or more places. Also called journey, travel, excursion. Examples: a business trip, a family vacation, a day trip to the beach.

candidates.label: TouristTrip
candidates.comment: An itinerary or journey undertaken by visitors for tourism purposes, often involving visits to multiple places of interest. Also called vacation itinerary, travel plan, sightseeing tour. Examples: a two-week European tour, a weekend getaway to a national park, a cruise itinerary.

candidates.label: BoatTrip
candidates.comment: A Trip representing a journey taken on a commercial ferry line or similar water transport. Also called ferry journey, boat excursion, water travel. Examples: "A ferry trip across the English Channel", "A sightseeing boat trip on the river", "A commercial fishing boat trip". Distinct from BoatReservation, which is the booking for the trip.

candidates.label: ChildrensEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized and designed for children. Also called kids' event, family event, youth gathering. Examples: A puppet show, a children's birthday party, a school play, a kids' festival.

candidates.label: Flight
candidates.comment: A Flight is a Trip representing an airline journey. Also called air travel, plane ride, air route. Examples: Flight BA249 from London to Rio, a domestic flight from New York to Chicago, a charter flight.

types.embedding_query_text: Setting: The place or type of surroundings where something is positioned or where an event takes place. Also called Environment, Location, Locale, Context. Examples: seedy underbelly of America.

chosen_type.label: Place
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Place class represents a physical location or environment, which is a good general fit for the OIE_TYPE 'Setting' and the example 'seedy underbelly of America'.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

candidates.label: Seat
candidates.comment: A specific seating location, often reserved, within an event venue or transportation. Also called reserved spot, seating assignment, chair, place. Examples: seat 12A on an airplane, row F seat 5 at a concert, a specific table at a restaurant.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

types.embedding_query_text: Trailer: A short promotional video for a film, television program, or video game. Also called Teaser, Promo video, Preview. Examples: gameplay trailers, two gameplay trailers.

chosen_type.label: VideoGameClip
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org VideoGameClip class explicitly mentions 'trailer' in its definition and examples, making it a perfect match for 'gameplay trailers'.

candidates.label: VideoGameClip
candidates.comment: A short segment or part of a video game, often used for promotional or highlight purposes. Also called game clip, gameplay footage, video game segment. Examples: a highlight reel from an e-sports match, a trailer showing a game's cutscene, a short recording of a player's achievement.

candidates.label: ScreeningEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving the public showing of a movie or other video content. Also called film screening, movie showing, video presentation, cinema event. Examples: a film festival screening, a premiere showing of a new movie, a public documentary viewing, a drive-in movie night.

candidates.label: Clip
candidates.comment: A short segment or part of a larger audio or video program. Also called segment, excerpt, snippet, short video. Examples: A news clip, a movie trailer, a highlight reel from a sports game, a sound bite. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is the broader category for any creative content.

candidates.label: MovieClip
candidates.comment: A MovieClip, as a CreativeWork Clip, is a short segment or part of a movie. Also called film clip, video clip, movie segment, film segment. Examples: a movie trailer, a deleted scene, a blooper reel, a short excerpt used in a review. Distinct from MovieSeries, which is a collection of related films.

candidates.label: TVClip
candidates.comment: A short segment or part of a television program. Also called TV segment, television excerpt, show clip, broadcast snippet. Examples: a highlight reel from a TV show, a news report segment, a commercial break.

types.embedding_query_text: Animal: A living organism that feeds on organic matter, typically having specialized sense organs and nervous system and able to respond rapidly to stimuli. Also called Creature, Beast, Fauna. Examples: alligators and flamingos.

chosen_type.label: Animal
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Animal class is a direct and accurate match for the OIE_TYPE definition and examples like 'alligators and flamingos'.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: Zoo
candidates.comment: A civic structure and facility where wild animals are housed, exhibited, and often bred for conservation and public education. Also called zoological garden, animal park, wildlife park. Examples: San Diego Zoo, London Zoo, Bronx Zoo.

candidates.label: BioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A fundamental Thing representing any biological, chemical, or biochemical substance or entity. Also called biochemical, chemical compound, biological entity, molecule. Examples: "A protein molecule", "A specific gene sequence", "A synthetic chemical compound", "DNA".

candidates.label: Taxon
candidates.comment: A cohesive biological unit representing a group of organisms, such as a species, genus, or family. Also called biological classification, taxonomic group, species, genus. Examples: Homo sapiens, Canis familiaris, Felidae (cat family), Plantae (plant kingdom).

candidates.label: VeterinaryCare
candidates.comment: A local business or organization providing medical services for animals. Also called vet clinic, animal hospital, veterinary practice. Examples: a local veterinary office, an emergency animal hospital, a mobile vet service.

types.embedding_query_text: DigitalContent: Any content that exists in the form of digital data. Also called Digital media, Electronic content, Digital assets. Examples: footage and images.

chosen_type.label: WebContent
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org WebContent class is a general type for digital content, including images and footage, making it a suitable fit for 'DigitalContent'.

candidates.label: WebContent
candidates.comment: A general type representing any content accessible via the web, including web pages, websites, and their elements. Also called web content item, online content, digital web asset. Examples: a blog post, an entire website, an image embedded on a page.

candidates.label: DigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A creative work representing an electronic file or document. Also called Electronic document, e-document, digital file, computer file. Examples: A PDF report, a Word document, a spreadsheet, an image file, an e-book. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is a broader category for any creative output.

candidates.label: TextDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A digital document primarily composed of textual content. Also called text file, digital document, e-document. Examples: a PDF report, a Word document, an e-book. Distinct from TextObject, which is a media object representing a text file, often for embedding or linking.

candidates.label: HealthTopicContent
candidates.comment: HealthTopicContent is web content about a specific aspect of a health topic, such as a medical condition, its symptoms, or treatments. Also called medical web content, health information article, wellness resource. Examples: an article explaining diabetes symptoms, a webpage detailing cancer treatments, a video on heart disease prevention.

candidates.label: DigitalDocumentPermission
candidates.comment: An intangible entity defining the access rights granted to a specific person or group for a particular digital document. Also called File permission, access control, document rights, sharing setting. Examples: "Read-only access for John Doe", "Edit permission for the Marketing Team", "View and comment access for all users". Distinct from DigitalDocumentPermissionType, which is an enumeration of possible permission types.

types.embedding_query_text: GroupOfPeople: A collection of individuals considered as a unit. Also called Team, Collective, Party, Crowd. Examples: teenage hackers, sacked workers, Analysts, players.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Organization class is the closest general type for a 'GroupOfPeople', encompassing both formal and informal groups like 'teenage hackers' or 'fans'.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: StatisticalPopulation
candidates.comment: A set of instances of a given type that satisfy specific constraints, used for statistical analysis. Also called statistical group, data population, sample group, target demographic. Examples: all persons with a home location in a specific city, all events occurring in a particular year, all news articles mentioning a certain keyword. Distinct from StatisticalVariable, which represents a measurable metric within a population.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

types.embedding_query_text: Profession: A paid occupation, especially one that involves prolonged training and a formal qualification. Also called Occupation, Career, Job, Vocation. Examples: developers.

chosen_type.label: Occupation
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Occupation class is a direct and accurate match for the OIE_TYPE definition and the example 'developers'.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

candidates.label: ProfessionalService
candidates.comment: ProfessionalService is a LocalBusiness type for providers of specialized services. Also called expert service, specialized service. Examples: a legal service, an accounting service, a dental practice, an architectural firm. Distinct from Service, which is a broader concept of an intangible offering.

candidates.label: SoftwareApplication
candidates.comment: A computer program designed to perform specific tasks for a user. Also called application, app, computer program, software. Examples: Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop, a mobile game, a web browser.

candidates.label: Attorney
candidates.comment: An Attorney is a LegalService professional who practices law, providing legal advice and representation. Also called lawyer, legal counsel, barrister, solicitor. Examples: a criminal defense attorney, a corporate lawyer, a family law solicitor, a public defender. Distinct from LegalService, which is the broader category of services provided by legal professionals.

candidates.label: Specialty
candidates.comment: Any branch of a field in which individuals develop specific expertise, typically through significant study and effort. Also called area of expertise, specialization, discipline, field. Examples: 'Cardiology' as a medical specialty, 'Corporate Law' as a legal specialty, 'Artificial Intelligence' as a computer science specialty.

types.embedding_query_text: GameplayStyle: A particular approach or characteristic manner of playing a video game. Also called Game genre, Play style, Game mechanics. Examples: sandbox gameplay.

chosen_type.label: GamePlayMode
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org GamePlayMode enumeration categorizes different ways or styles of playing a game, which aligns well with 'GameplayStyle' and 'sandbox gameplay'.

candidates.label: GamePlayMode
candidates.comment: A GamePlayMode is an Enumeration indicating whether a game is multi-player, co-op, or single-player. Also called player mode, game type. Examples: SinglePlayer, MultiPlayer, CoOp.

candidates.label: PlayGameAction
candidates.comment: PlayGameAction is a ConsumeAction specifically representing the act of playing a video game. Also called gaming, video gaming, playing a digital game. Examples: playing "Minecraft", playing "Fortnite", playing "Chess" online, playing a mobile game. Distinct from PlayAction, which is a broader act of playing or performing.

candidates.label: VideoGameSeries
candidates.comment: A sequence of related video games, often sharing a common storyline, characters, or gameplay mechanics. Also called game franchise, video game saga, game series. Examples: The Final Fantasy series, The Elder Scrolls series, Grand Theft Auto series.

candidates.label: Game
candidates.comment: A Game is a CreativeWork representing a rule-governed recreational activity, often involving players assuming roles in a fictional setting. Also called pastime, play, recreational activity. Examples: A board game like Chess, a video game like Minecraft, a role-playing game like Dungeons & Dragons, a card game like Poker.

candidates.label: VideoGame
candidates.comment: An electronic game that involves human interaction with a user interface to generate visual feedback on a video device. Also called computer game, console game, digital game. Examples: Super Mario Bros., The Legend of Zelda, Call of Duty.

types.embedding_query_text: GameWorld: The fictional universe in which a video game takes place, often featuring interactive environments. Also called Virtual world, Fictional world, Game environment, Open world. Examples: vast open worlds.

chosen_type.label: GameWorld
chosen_type.definition: The fictional universe in which a video game takes place, often featuring interactive environments.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate directly represents a game world. 'Vast open worlds' are fictional environments within a creative work, making 'CreativeWork' an appropriate parent.

candidates.label: VideoGame
candidates.comment: An electronic game that involves human interaction with a user interface to generate visual feedback on a video device. Also called computer game, console game, digital game. Examples: Super Mario Bros., The Legend of Zelda, Call of Duty.

candidates.label: Game
candidates.comment: A Game is a CreativeWork representing a rule-governed recreational activity, often involving players assuming roles in a fictional setting. Also called pastime, play, recreational activity. Examples: A board game like Chess, a video game like Minecraft, a role-playing game like Dungeons & Dragons, a card game like Poker.

candidates.label: VideoGameSeries
candidates.comment: A sequence of related video games, often sharing a common storyline, characters, or gameplay mechanics. Also called game franchise, video game saga, game series. Examples: The Final Fantasy series, The Elder Scrolls series, Grand Theft Auto series.

candidates.label: GameServer
candidates.comment: A GameServer is an Intangible server that facilitates game interaction in a multiplayer game. Also called game host, multiplayer server. Examples: A dedicated server for an online game, a private game server for friends, a public game server for a large community.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

types.embedding_query_text: Medium: A means or channel of communication or expression. Also called Channel, Format, Art form, Mode. Examples: interactive medium, film, song.

chosen_type.label: MediaObject
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org MediaObject class represents various forms of media like 'film' and 'song', making it the best fit for the OIE_TYPE 'Medium' given the examples.

candidates.label: CommunicateAction
candidates.comment: The act of transmitting information to another person or entity through a specific medium. Also called communication, conveying information, interacting. Examples: Sending an email, making a phone call, giving a speech, writing a letter. Distinct from InteractAction, which is a broader category of actions involving interaction.

candidates.label: Conversation
candidates.comment: A series of one or more messages exchanged between individuals or organizations on a specific topic. Also called discussion, dialogue, chat, discourse. Examples: An email thread, a text message exchange, a forum discussion, a spoken dialogue. Distinct from Comment, which is a single remark on an item.

candidates.label: MediaObject
candidates.comment: A creative work representing a media object like an image, video, audio, or text, which can be embedded or downloaded. Also called digital media asset, multimedia file, content object. Examples: a JPEG image file, an MP4 video, an MP3 audio track, a PDF document. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is a broader category for any creative output.

candidates.label: ImageObject
candidates.comment: An ImageObject is a media object creative work representing an image file. Also called picture, photo, graphic, visual. Examples: a JPEG photograph, a PNG illustration, a GIF animation. Distinct from VideoObject, which is a video file, and AudioObject, which is an audio file.

candidates.label: Message
candidates.comment: A creative work representing a single communication from a sender to one or more recipients. Also called communication, dispatch, note, email. Examples: an email, a text message, a direct message on social media, a voicemail.

types.embedding_query_text: Boundary: A line or limit that marks the extent of something. Also called Limit, Edge, Frontier, Threshold. Examples: technical and gameplay boundaries.

chosen_type.label: Boundary
chosen_type.definition: A line or limit that marks the extent of something.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate directly represents a 'Boundary'. 'Technical and gameplay boundaries' are abstract, intangible concepts, making 'Intangible' the most appropriate parent.

candidates.label: LegalValueLevel
candidates.comment: LegalValueLevel is an enumeration of possible levels for the legal validity or authority of a legislation. Also called legislative authority level, legal hierarchy, law's binding power. Examples: 'Primary', 'Secondary', 'Tertiary', 'Advisory'.

candidates.label: Distance
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Distance represents a numerical value combined with a unit of length. Also called length, extent, span, separation. Examples: "10 km", "5 miles", "300 meters", "2 feet".

candidates.label: PostalCodeRangeSpecification
candidates.comment: A PostalCodeRangeSpecification is a StructuredValue indicating a range of postal codes, defined by a beginning and ending code. Also called zip code range, postcode boundary. Examples: 90210-90215, 00000-99999, a range of postal codes for a delivery zone.

candidates.label: BoardingPolicyType
candidates.comment: An Enumeration representing different policies used by airlines for boarding passengers. Also called airline boarding rule, boarding group type, flight boarding policy. Examples: "Zone boarding", "Group boarding", "Priority boarding", "Family boarding".

candidates.label: VideoGameClip
candidates.comment: A short segment or part of a video game, often used for promotional or highlight purposes. Also called game clip, gameplay footage, video game segment. Examples: a highlight reel from an e-sports match, a trailer showing a game's cutscene, a short recording of a player's achievement.

types.embedding_query_text: BusinessModel: A plan for the successful operation of a business, identifying sources of revenue, the intended customer base, products, and financing details. Also called Operating model, Revenue model, Business strategy. Examples: live service model.

chosen_type.label: BusinessModel
chosen_type.definition: A plan for the successful operation of a business, identifying sources of revenue, the intended customer base, products, and financing details.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate directly represents a 'BusinessModel'. A 'live service model' is an intangible concept or plan, making 'Intangible' the most appropriate parent.

candidates.label: ProductModel
candidates.comment: A ProductModel is a Product representing a datasheet or vendor specification of a prototypical product description. Also called product prototype, product specification, product blueprint. Examples: the technical specifications for a new laptop model, a design document for a car engine, a vendor's product data sheet, a conceptual product design.

candidates.label: BusinessFunction
candidates.comment: A BusinessFunction is an Enumeration specifying the type of activity or access rights offered by an organization through an offer. Also called commercial activity, service type, transaction type. Examples: Sell, LeaseOut, Repair, ProvideService, Buy.

candidates.label: 3DModel
candidates.comment: A 3DModel, as a MediaObject under CreativeWork, represents some kind of three-dimensional content, which may have various digital encodings. Also called 3D content, digital model, virtual model. Examples: A CAD file of an engine part, a character model for a video game, a geospatial terrain model, an architectural rendering.

candidates.label: MedicalBusiness
candidates.comment: A local business operating for medical purposes, which can be physical or virtual. Also called healthcare business, medical practice, health services provider. Examples: a dental office, a physical therapy clinic, a telemedicine service, a diagnostic lab. Distinct from LocalBusiness, which is a broader category for any local business.

candidates.label: PaymentMethod
candidates.comment: A PaymentMethod is an intangible entity representing a standardized procedure for transferring monetary amounts for a purchase. Also called payment option, mode of payment, transaction method. Examples: Cash, CreditCard, BankTransfer, PayPal. Distinct from PaymentMethodType, which is a generic classification.

types.embedding_query_text: CulturalTrends: General directions or movements in the development of culture, including aspects like music, entertainment, and societal norms. Also called Societal trends, Cultural shifts, Pop culture trends, Fads. Examples: music, entertainment, societal, political, celebrity, and online culture trends.

chosen_type.label: CulturalTrend
chosen_type.definition: General directions or movements in the development of culture, including aspects like music, entertainment, and societal norms.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate directly represents 'CulturalTrends'. These are abstract, intangible movements, making 'Intangible' the most appropriate parent for this new type.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: SocialEvent
candidates.comment: An event primarily focused on social interaction and entertainment. Also called party, gathering, social function, get-together. Examples: a birthday party, a wedding reception, a community picnic, a networking mixer.

candidates.label: TheaterEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing a live performance in a theater. Also called stage play, theatrical show, drama performance. Examples: a Broadway musical, a local community play, a Shakespearean tragedy.

candidates.label: DanceEvent
candidates.comment: A DanceEvent is a social gathering or organized occasion primarily focused on dancing. Also called dance party, ball, disco, social dance. Examples: A salsa night, a wedding reception with dancing, a school prom, a folk dance festival.

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

types.embedding_query_text: Software: The programs and other operating information used by a computer. Also called Computer program, Application, Code, System. Examples: interactive software.

chosen_type.label: SoftwareApplication
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org SoftwareApplication class is a direct and accurate match for the OIE_TYPE definition, with 'software' explicitly listed as an alternative name.

candidates.label: SoftwareApplication
candidates.comment: A computer program designed to perform specific tasks for a user. Also called application, app, computer program, software. Examples: Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop, a mobile game, a web browser.

candidates.label: OperatingSystem
candidates.comment: An OperatingSystem, as a SoftwareApplication, is system software that manages computer hardware and software resources. Also called OS, system software, platform. Examples: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is a general application program.

candidates.label: WebApplication
candidates.comment: A software application that runs on a web server and is accessed by users via a web browser. Also called web app, online application, browser-based application. Examples: Gmail, Google Docs, Facebook.

candidates.label: SoftwareSourceCode
candidates.comment: The human-readable instructions written in a programming language that define a software application. Also called source code, program code, script, code snippet. Examples: Python script for data analysis, C++ code for a game engine, HTML/CSS/JavaScript for a website, a Java class file.

candidates.label: Code
candidates.comment: Computer programming source code, such as full solutions, snippets, scripts, or templates. Also called programming code, software code, source program. Examples: Python script, Java application, HTML template, SQL query.
